'''Tatiana Korcová'''. (7 March 1937  –  12 November 1997) was a Slovak [[physicist]] specializing in the study of [[solar wind]]s.

Tatiana Korcová was born on 7 March 1937 in [[Trenčianska Teplá]]. She studied Physics and Chemistry at the [[Comenius University]], graduating in 1959.<ref name=":0" /> Following graduation she briefly worked as a high school teacher in [[Trenčín]]. In 1963 she joined the  [[Constantine the Philosopher University in Nitra]], where she spent her entire career.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=https://www.mat.savba.sk/MATEMATICI/matematici.php?cislo=112 |title = doc. RNDr. Tatiana Korcová, CSc.
 |access-date=2023-10-09 |website=www.mat.savba.sk}}</ref>

Korcová studied cosmic radiation and high-energy particles in close cooperation with [[Slovak Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1985 she was awarded the [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree by the academy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teraz.sk |date=2017-03-07 |title=Slovenská fyzička zasvätila život výskumu kozmického žiarenia |url=https://www.teraz.sk/magazin/tatiana-korcova-sa-venovala-vyskumu-ko/247307-clanok.html |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=TERAZ.sk |language=sk}}</ref> Korcová's [[habilitation]] thesis, which she passed in 1994, was on the issue of long-term solar wind variations.<ref name=":0" />

Tatiana Korcová died on 12 November 1997 at the age of 60 in [[Bratislava]].<ref name=":0" />
